business: A manufacturer of food and beverage products. It receives materials, makes, packs and tests product, and releases it for despatch, through its own factories and through outside manufacturers. What a product is and what goes into it is held by CPG - Product Definition; this model holds the logistics of making finished products from those ingredients.

in_scope.statement: Receiving materials from suppliers, and assessing the suppliers
Defining how products are made — the steps, the settings and the recipes
The places in each factory down to the shop floor, and the machines in them
Making product, and what each batch actually used and produced
Testing, recording problems, putting them right, and releasing product
Tracing any batch back to its ingredients and forward to where it went
Stock held at the organisation's own sites
Product made or packed by outside manufacturers
Packing, and the levels a product is packed in for handling — unit, case and pallet
The sites that suppliers and outside manufacturers make and ship from

Turning ingredients into finished products: the logistics of receiving, making, packing and moving them, built on the product and the hierarchy of products and ingredients held by CPG - Product Definition

out_of_scope.statement: Trade spending, promotions and pricing with retailers
What happens on the shelf in store
Market share and sales data bought from research firms
Research and development before a product is formally defined
Defining products — what they are made from, what they must be, how long they last and what their packs say
The total cost of poor quality, and any other cost worked out by adding up what happened
Household and cleaning products, personal care and cosmetics, pet care and beauty
out_of_scope.owned_by: A later extension of this model

assumptions.statement: The factory, laboratory, quality and maintenance systems already in place stay in place. This model holds what they record; it does not replace them.
Material held by a supplier or outside manufacturer is theirs. It becomes the organisation's on receipt, and the organisation holds no stock at any party it does not operate.
Something bought as an ingredient or part may be another company's finished product. What it is made from is theirs and may not be known here.

The product definition — what a product is made from, what it must be, how long it lasts and what its pack says — is held by CPG - Product Definition. This model refers to a product and does not define it again.
A manufacturing bill of materials is read as the formulation held in CPG - Product Definition. This model holds how a batch compares with it: what was used, and in what quantity.

Food traceability duties differ by market. The United States, the United Kingdom and the European Union are the sample markets, and other markets come in as further requirements, not as a different design.
Costs are not held. What each stoppage, failure, rework and complaint was is recorded; adding them up is a calculation outside this model.

questions_unanswered.note: Is finished output identified individually, or only by batch? The model supports both; how much of Instances is used depends on the answer.
What proportion of output is made by outside manufacturers? Where it is most of it, the organisation holds little production record of its own.
